data.cultural_impact: The name Ck has its roots in Hindu mythology, where it is believed to represent the deity Chandra, also known as the moon god. In Hindu culture, the moon is considered the symbol of peace, tranquility, and nourishment. The name Ck holds this spiritual connection and is associated with these profound cultural values.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ck holds immense spiritual significance in Hinduism as it is believed to be derived from the name of the moon god. In Hinduism, the cyclical nature of the moon signifies life's continuous journey, renewal, and transformation. The name Ck echoes this profound spiritual symbolism, reminding us of the importance of cyclical living and encouraging us to embrace the ever-changing nature of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name "CK" in Hindu tradition is believed to represent the union of consciousness (Chit) and knowledge (Knowledge). This symbolizes the pursuit of wisdom and self-realization. It is a reminder to seek inner wisdom and knowledge to attain spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Chola dynasty inscriptions mentioning the name Ck. A notable inscription is that of Rajaraja Chola I, dating to 1012 CE, which mentions a gift to the god Shiva at the temple town of Thanjavur. The inscription uses the name Ck as a title for a certain official.

The name Ck also appears in the records of the Maratha king Shivaji (1627-1680 CE) as the name of a Subahdar (a military governor) in the Deccan region. The inscription referring to him is dated to 1657 CE.
